title: Week in Orbit
summary: The space and defense sectors are experiencing a mix of growth and bureaucratic headwinds. As companies pivot towards new opportunities, the military's appetite for innovation faces challenges from regulatory frameworks.

themes.title: NASA's Moon Base Ventures
themes.body: Redwire is eyeing landers and power systems to support NASA's lunar ambitions. This move underscores the increasing commercial interest in lunar infrastructure as the agency ramps up its Artemis program.

themes.title: Military Space Dynamics
themes.body: The anticipated military space boom is encountering friction within the Beltway, highlighting the complexities of defense procurement. As budgets increase, so do the challenges of aligning innovation with governmental processes.

themes.title: Funding and Investments Surge
themes.body: Palantir's $480M extension and True Anomaly's $190M Series C reflect a robust funding environment for space-tech ventures. This trend indicates a growing confidence in the commercial viability of space applications.

themes.title: AI's Role in Defense
themes.body: The integration of AI into defense strategies is gaining momentum, as evidenced by the DAF's AI workforce plan. This shift suggests a recognition that advanced technologies will be crucial in maintaining competitive advantages in space.
